lines.text: Every climb, Jake blamed his legs.
Burning thighs, sore shoulders, last in the group.
Then a guide stopped him at the trailhead and looked at his poles.
Way too long. Hands up by his chin.
Stand straight, grip the handle, and set the pole so your elbow sits at ninety degrees.
Shorter going uphill, longer going down.
Next hike? He led the group.
Save this before your next climb.
